title: Mitigation playbook and comms plan for Ember release: risk gating and rollback readiness
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: Create a concise, actionable mitigation playbook and stakeholder-facing communications bundle to ensure Ember release (runtime-2.4) can be gated, rolled back, or hot-fixed with minimal customer disruption. Scope: release blockers checklist, pre-launch risk signoff, automated rollback knobs, incident comms templates for SEV1/SEV2/SEV3, on-call runbook snippets, and owner matrix. Not in scope: full QA matrix (owned by ENG QA) and long-form marketing collateral.
acceptance_criteria: Launch risk checklist reviewed and signed by ENG leads, SRE, Security, and Docs
Rollback procedure validated in staging with a test rollback drill and documented failure modes
Incident comms templates approved and staged in the comms repo with variables and escalation steps
Release notes entry created and linked; legal & privacy confirmations completed
On-call owners have been added to the runbook and a dry-run completed
checklist: Finalize pre-launch blockers list and owners
Confirm metrics and dashboards are instrumented for new endpoints
Create feature flags and emergency kill-switch routes
Prepare staged rollback artifact (previous model binary and config) in S3
Draft release notes and publish draft to Docs for review
Schedule release-day war room and calendar invite with stakeholders
Prepare post-launch monitoring checklist with thresholds and alert destinations
rollback_plan: Step 1: Detect — automated health checks (latency P90 > 800ms or error rate > 2%) trigger SEV1 alert
Step 2: Triage — on-call SRE to validate alerts within 10 minutes using trace links and recent deploys
Step 3: Contain — if degradations confirmed, flip feature flag for Ember feature to 'off' (immediate) and route traffic to fallback model variant
Step 4: Rollback — deploy last-known-good release (runtime-2.3) via blue/green rollback pipeline; target MTTR < 20 minutes
Step 5: Post-rollback validation — run smoke tests and synthetic traces for 15 minutes; if stable, notify customers and resume scheduled postmortem
Step 6: Postmortem — capture root cause, mitigation, and release gates to prevent recurrence
rollout_strategy: Canary 5% for first 30 minutes with KV-cache warmed for high-traffic prefixes
If metrics stable, expand to 25% for next 30 minutes
A/B routing for dedicated accounts with opt-in list (customer tier flagged) to avoid skews
Hold points: after each expansion, PM/SRE signoff required and health checks must remain within thresholds
Automatic throttle: if any critical metric violates thresholds during expansion, auto-hold and trigger rollback plan

Customer guidance: We are rolling back to runtime-2.3 and will follow up with ETA. Affected customers: list_link. Next update: in 15 minutes. Contact: oncall@redwood.com; slack #sevs

SEV2 template: [Timestamp] SEV2: Partial degradation — increased latency observed for >10% of requests. Current status: Mitigating via feature flag. Customer guidance: We may see intermittent errors; recommend retry/backoff. Next update: in 30 minutes. Owner: SRE lead. Contact: se-help@redwood.com

SEV3 template: [Timestamp] SEV3: Low-impact anomaly detected — elevated tail latency for single region. Current status: Monitoring. Customer guidance: No action required. Root cause investigation ongoing. Next update: in 2 hours. Contact: pager team

notes_for_release_notes_team: Summary line: Introducing Ember optimizations in runtime-2.4 — faster KV cache priming and lower tail latency for generation workloads (canary-first rollout).
Known limitations: In initial rollout, some accounts may see temporary increased cold-start latencies; automatic rollback is in place for rapid mitigation.
Customer-facing guidance: Recommend adding retry/backoff and using dedicated model variants for critical flows during first 48 hours after rollout.
